types.name: LogRingBuffer
types.doc:
Ring buffer retained for post-crash log recovery. Producers are every
thread in the process, so the slot write and the index advance have to be
one atomic step — a mutex, not a pair of atomics.

members.name: GetAll
members.doc:
Best-effort snapshot. The crash handler runs on the faulting thread,
which may itself hold m_mutex, so a failed lock reads on anyway rather
than deadlocking and losing the dump entirely.

types.name: LogLevel
types.doc:
UE's verbosities under the engine's older names: Trace is VeryVerbose,
Debug is Verbose, Info is Log. Display sits between Log and Warning — a line
the developer using the editor should see by default, where Info is detail
for the log file and a bug report.

members.name: frame
members.doc:
Stamped by Logger::Log: the engine frame the line was written on and a
small stable id of the writing thread, so a line can be matched to a
Tracy capture or a Visual Logger frame and to the thread that wrote it.

types.name: ELogLinePrefix
types.doc:
Which of those the file and console lines print, off by default so the line
format stays what tools already parse: `log prefix frame thread` in the
console, `--logprefix=frame,thread`, or `LinePrefix=Frame,Thread` under
[Core.Log]. `none` clears it.

members.name: Apply

One `<category> <verbosity>` instruction, as `log`, -LogCmds and
[Core.Log] give it. `global` (or `all`) reaches every category,
`reset` restores the declared level. A category that is not registered
yet — a game module or plugin that loads later — takes the level when
it registers. False for an unknown verbosity.

members.name: ApplyConfig
members.doc:

members.name: ResetAll
members.doc: Every category back to its declared level, pending overrides dropped.

members.name: RegisterConsoleCommand
members.doc:
Registers the `log` console command: `log` lists every category and its
level, `log <category> <level>` sets one, `log <category> reset` restores
the level it was declared with. Called once during engine init.

members.name: CrashFlush
members.doc:
The crash path's flush: the process may already be broken and another
thread may hold this sink's lock forever, so it must never block on
it and never allocate. Defaults to Flush for sinks that hold nothing.

members.name: IsSlow
members.doc:
A sink whose Write can take milliseconds (a console on a pipe nobody
reads, a terminal). The Logger queues its lines for one writer thread
instead of calling Write under the lock every logging thread shares, so
a slow console cannot stall the render thread behind a worker's burst.
Order is kept (one queue, one writer) and Logger::Flush waits for it.
A sink that answers true must tolerate Write from that thread.

members.name: ConsoleSink
members.signature: ConsoleSink(bool useColors = true, bool showLocation = true, bool allToStderr = false) : m_useColors(useColors && !allToStderr), m_showLocation(showLocation), m_allToStderr(allToStderr)
members.doc:
`allToStderr` keeps stdout for a protocol: the editor's --mcp-stdio
speaks JSON-RPC on it, one message per line, and a log line or a colour
escape in between is a corrupt message to the client.

types.name: FileSink
types.doc:
Lines land in a memory buffer and reach the disk from a flusher thread
every 200 ms, when the buffer fills, on any Error/Fatal line, on Flush,
and from the crash handler's pre-report hook — never with a syscall per
line. The old sink wrote std::endl per message, one flush each, which
was a measurable share of a Debug frame under the render-init spam. The
file is opened shared-read so the crash reporter's tail copy and a tail
tool still see it mid-session.

No thread that logs ever waits on the disk. The flusher opens the file,
swaps the buffer out under the lock and writes it with the lock released;
an Error line only wakes it. The lock used to be held across fwrite and
fflush, and on a disk taking seconds per write (a project on a busy HDD)
every logging thread — the render thread included — froze behind it: the
owner's 14 s and 19 s "submit" stalls were the render thread waiting to
append one line. A disk that takes nothing for long enough costs lines,
counted in the file, never a frame.

members.name: SetFloodGuard
members.doc:
The flood guard: a category that writes more than `linesPerSecond` lines
in each of `seconds` consecutive seconds gets one warning naming its
busiest call site. Only call sites with a source file are counted, so a
release build (which compiles none in) pays nothing. 0 turns it off.

members.name: ResetFloodGuard
members.doc: Forgets every category's window and warning, so a test starts clean.

members.name: __attribute__
members.signature: __attribute__((format(printf, 6, 7))) void LogFormat(LogLevel level, const std::string& category, const char* file, int line, const char* fmt, ...)
members.doc:
Argument 1 is the implicit this, so the format string is 6 and the
variadic list starts at 7. A wrong specifier is undefined behaviour at
run time; the attribute makes it a -Wformat warning at the call site.

members.name: Flush
members.doc:
Waits (at most two seconds) for the slow sinks' queue to reach its
sinks, then flushes every sink. A crash or fatal path that must see its
last line on the console calls this first.

members.name: CrashFlush
members.doc:
What the crash handler runs before it copies the log tail: best
effort, no allocation, and never a wait on a lock the crashing thread
itself may hold.

members.name: TerminateAfterFatal
members.doc:
What MOWO_LOG_FATAL runs after it has logged the line: puts every sink on
disk, writes a crash report through the crash handler (so the dump, the
log tail and the reporter UI behave as for any other fatal) and aborts.
Never returns, and never reached by a bare Log(LogLevel::Fatal, ...), which
stays a line for callers that unwind on their own.

members.name: ResolveLogsDir
members.doc:
Where the file sink writes: <project>/Saved/Logs when a project is
open, else <state root>/<Product>/Saved/Logs (Launcher, headless
self-tests, packaged games with no writable project).

members.name: Initialize
members.doc:
Opens the console + file sinks and rotates old Mowo_*.log files out.
Release builds keep both sinks OFF and the threshold at Warning
unless -log is on the command line or the game's Config sets
logging.enabled=true (the bUseLoggingInShipping model).

members.name: PruneOldLogs
members.signature: static void PruneOldLogs(const std::filesystem::path& logsDir, size_t keep)
members.doc: Deletes the oldest Mowo_*.log / mowo_*.log files beyond `keep`.

members.name: LatestLogPath
members.doc:
<logsDir>/Mowo-latest.log: a name that always leads to the newest
session's log, for tooling and crash reports that cannot know a pid and
a timestamp. It is a hard link to the live file (a symbolic link where
that fails), so it shows the session as it is written. Several hosts
sharing one logs folder (editor plus PIE clients) race for it and the
last one to start wins. The `Mowo_` prefix pruning looks for is not in
its name, so pruning never counts or removes it.

members.name: UpdateLatestLink
members.signature: static bool UpdateLatestLink(const std::filesystem::path& logsDir, const std::filesystem::path& target)
members.doc:
Points LatestLogPath(logsDir) at `target`; false when neither kind of
link could be made (a file system without them, or another process
holding the old name open).

members.name: GetLogFilePath
members.doc: Absolute path of the file sink Initialize opened; empty without one.

types.name: FLogRateLimiter
types.doc:
One call site's budget: the first line passes, then at most one per
interval. A line that passes after some were held back is followed by a
count of them, so a rate-limited warning still says how often it fired.

free.name: ParseLogLinePrefix
free.doc:
A comma or space separated list of frame / thread / none; false on a word it
does not know, leaving `flags` untouched.

free.name: GetLogProfilerForward
free.doc:
How much of the log reaches the profiler's message timeline when Tracy is
compiled in: 0 nothing, 1 warnings and above (the default), 2 every line.

free.name: InstallScreenMessageMirror
free.doc:
Surfaces Message Log entries on screen the way UE's output log errors do: an
observer that forwards by ui.ScreenMessages.MessageLogSeverity (1 errors,
2 errors and warnings) and ui.ScreenMessages.MessageLogPages into
FScreenMessages. The key is the text, so an error posted every frame is one
line with a repeat count. Returns the observer handle for RemoveObserver.

members.name: SerializeRecording
members.doc:
A recording is the ring written as one binary blob (magic, version, then
every entry with its shapes), so a bug seen on a server or a client can be
opened later in the viewer. Frames and times are stored as recorded.
Loading replaces the ring unless `append`; entries get fresh serials and
bypass IsEnabled, since a viewer opens a recording with recording off.
False on an unreadable, truncated or newer-version file, leaving the ring
untouched.
